referents.why: 2ms suffix on 'word' in cl3 ('as your word'), inside Moses's turn1, which is spoken to Pharaoh (Exo.8.5#w4). The word meant is Pharaoh's 'Tomorrow' in cl1. Masculine singular agrees.

1cp 'our' in 'the LORD our God' is the speaker's community, Israel. No candidate names Israel. The builder's cl2s (Moses alone, singular) cannot carry a first-person plural, so the builder referent is rejected.
referents.category: first-person plural with no candidate group

referents.why: 3ms implied subject of wayyiqtol cl0. Moses has just spoken to Pharaoh (Exo.8.5), and the one who answers 'Tomorrow' is Pharaoh. Masculine singular agrees.
3ms implied subject of wayyiqtol cl2, 'Moses replied'. Pharaoh has just spoken to Moses in cl0, and Moses answers. Masculine singular agrees.
2ms implied subject of yiqtol cl4 ('you may know'). Inside Moses's speech the addressee is Pharaoh.

links.why: Object clause of 'you may know': the clause is what is known (ki after yada), not a reason.
links.category: object clause after a verb of knowing

links.why: cl0 is the verse's first clause, so a narrative 'and then' cannot run from cl4 back to it. The then link runs forward to the next clause on the narrative line.
cl1 is inside Pharaoh's speech. A wayyiqtol continues the nearest clause before it that is not inside a speech, which is cl0. Replaced by cl0 then cl2.
links.category: narrative link from inside a speech

links.why: lemaan with yiqtol ('you may know') states what the assent is for.
wayyiqtol cl2 continues the narrative line from the frame cl0, the nearest preceding clause outside a speech.

groups.why: Pharaoh's answer 'Tomorrow'. Sender changed from slot cl0s to its referent, Pharaoh. Addressee added: Moses, who asked the question in Exo.8.5.
Moses's reply: 'as your word' and the purpose clause 'so that you may know'. Sender changed from slot cl2s to Moses. Addressee added: Pharaoh.

none_fit.what: A reply to a question has no link type.
Moses's assent to Pharaoh's stated word is a reply to a proposal, and no link type carries assent or acceptance. 'as' (just as) compares an action to a saying, which this is not.

cant_tell.what: What the purpose clause cl4 is for: Moses's assent (cl3), or the removal of the frogs by his prayer
cant_tell.why: The verse names the knowing but not the act it is for. The purpose link to cl3 is kept as the nearest act; the removal is not stated in this verse.
